subject: Cross-border data transfer assurances / TIA details
messages:
From: Linda Sorensen <linda.sorensen@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 09:14:00 +0200
Subject: Initial TIA / cross-border questions for Redwood

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking the call last week. As part of our procurement review for cloud-based inference providers we need a short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) and some supporting evidence to satisfy our EU Data Protection Officer and the procurement panel.

Can you provide a completed copy of the attached questionnaire (we've flagged mandatory questions) and any evidence you can share about where customer data is processed, subcontractors, SCCs or alternative transfer safeguards, and your technical controls for minimizing international exposure (encryption in transit/at rest, key custody, pseudonymization measures)?

Key ask: we'd like a usable PDF we can attach to the DPIA the team is assembling, and any internal attestation we can put in our vendor risk system. Timeline: ideally by EOD next Friday (2026-05-01) — can you confirm?

Thanks,
Linda
Linda Sorensen
Head of Legal & Privacy
Acme Health

Attachment: TIA_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Sorensen <linda.sorensen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 11:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Initial TIA / cross-border questions for Redwood

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear ask and deadline. We're on it.

Quick plan:
- We'll complete the questionnaire directly in the sheet you attached and return a flattened PDF for your DPIA.
- Marcus will assemble the technical artefacts (architecture diagrams + processing location map).
- Marissa will pull our contractual evidence (SCC templates, data processing addendum references).
- Karthik will coordinate a brief attestation note for procurement and confirm the timeline.

Small clarification: can you confirm whether Acme needs plaintext data flow diagrams (i.e., customer PII samples masked) or a high-level topology is sufficient? We want to avoid sharing anything unnecessary.

We'll aim to deliver an internal package by 2026-05-01 and can do a short walkthrough call on 2026-05-04 if helpful.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2026 14:37:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Initial TIA / cross-border questions for Redwood

Naomi / team - taking point on the tech pack. Draft summary below (will attach formal PDF and diagrams):

- Processing locations: Primary inference hosting in eu-central (Frankfurt) for EU accounts; fallthrough routing to us-east for customers who select global routing or Dedicated deployments. We will provide a per-customer processing map in the deliverable.
- Subprocessors: cloud compute providers (listed in DPA), monitoring/logging vendor (logops@example.com), analytics provider (masked). We will include signed subprocessors list and effective dates.
- SCCs and safeguards: Redwood uses EU Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-processor + processor-processor as applicable) as default for cross-border transfers; template attached (SCCs-reference.docx). We also support Data Processing Agreements with explicit SCC annexes for enterprise contracts.
- Technical controls: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, per-tenant KMS integration (customer-managed keys available for Private/Dedicated), KV-cache obfuscation, automatic prefix masking for logs.
- Minimization: default retention windows, token-level truncation on request, ability to pin data residency per account.

I'm attaching: redwood-TIA-summary.pdf (high-level narrative + map), SCCs-reference.docx.

Will also drop a Drive link with diagrams and a checklist for your DPIA reviewer.

Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-TIA-summary.pdf, SCCs-reference.docx
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3redwood-tia-evidence

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Sorensen <linda.sorensen@acmehealth.com>, privacy@acmehealth.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, DPIA Consultant <dpiaconsultant@civsec.eu>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 16:22:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border data transfer assurances / TIA details

Linda — please find the attached package for your DPIA reviewer. Summary of what we've provided below and next steps.

Package contents (attached and Drive):
- Completed TIA_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (we filled mandatory fields and added explanatory notes).
- redwood-TIA-summary.pdf: narrative of transfer landscape, processing locations, risk mitigations.
- SCCs-reference.docx: our standard SCC annex and execution checklist.
- Drive folder with architecture diagrams and per-region processing map.

Key notes for your team:
- For EU-only residency please select the EU data residency option in the contract; we'll ensure processing stays within Frankfurt region and appropriate SCCs will be in place for any necessary subprocessors.
- For customer-managed keys / HIPAA-enabled deployments we have a separate support onboarding flow (we've included the checklist in the Drive).

Timeline: confirm receipt and whether the DPIA reviewer wants a 30-minute walkthrough next week. If you need an enterprise attestation letter signed by legal, Marissa can prepare that once we have the PO/contract path.

Thanks — happy to refine anything for Acme's reviewer.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: TIA_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (completed), redwood-TIA-summary.pdf, SCCs-reference.docx
